verdict.tagline: A sprawling wasteland of unmatched choice hobbled by unstable tech.
for_you_if: you want deep roleplaying choices and branching quest outcomes
you enjoy exploring a rich, reactive desert wasteland

you are unwilling to troubleshoot crashes and modern hardware setup
you want main quests that continue after completion

claims.claim: Reviewers note that save files can become corrupted.

citations.review_text: As good as I remember playing it as a child back in the day even better on PC, though I ran into the strangest bug. The game won't let me play on Fullscreen mode unless I change my monitor setting to native 1920 x 1080p. I usually play games on 1280 x 720p so it runs smoothly and I get better frames etc. FNV doesn't let me do that. So I set textures to med and everything else on low to med and shadows off. I also had to restart a new game because it crashed and corrupted my game.

The game itself is actually really good; however, I cannot recommend it in the slightest, even when it's on a massive discount, purely because of how unstable it is. Your save can sometimes just randomly get corrupted for no apparent reason, and there won't be anything you can do to prevent it or fix it.

My free time is far too precious to be wasted on a game that doesn't respect my time.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the high degree of player choice and multiple branching paths available in quests and endings.

citations.review_text: New Vegas is easily one my favourite Fallout games I've ever played. The story gives you loads of freedom, your choices actually matter, and every faction feels like it has its own strengths and flaws. The world is packed with interesting characters, memorable quests, and plenty to explore. Despite showing its age, the modding community are still going to keep this game running. If you enjoy games where your decisions shape the outcome, New Vegas is definitely worth playing. If you are eager to play now then I highly recommend installing the Viva New Vegas modpack that improves the gameplay, fixes bugs and a few other missing contents but still keeping the New Vegas vibe. Otherwise wait for the remasters from Bethesda.

Although I would recommend this game to anyone, this version has quite a few issues, especially the bugs. Some quests can become difficult or even impossible to complete without using console commands, and the game also crashes or freezes randomly from time to time.

That said, the story is absolutely fantastic. I spent most of my time playing the side quests, and I enjoyed every minute of them. They add so much depth to the world and are easily one of the game's biggest strengths.

As of writing this review, there is news that Fallout: New Vegas may be getting a remaster. If that happens and the developers improve the graphics while fixing the bugs, it could become the definitive way to experience the game.

For now, many of the bugs and crashes can be resolved with mods, so it really comes down to whether you want to wait for a potential remaster or jump into the current version.

The thing I loved most about this game is the incredible amount of player choice. Whether it's how you approach quests, interact with characters, or shape the story, the freedom is unmatched. If you enjoy games that give you meaningful choices and multiple ways to play, you'll absolutely love Fallout: New Vegas.

I only bought this game recently and I haven't played that much yet but this is already fully worth the money I spent on it. I really love just how many choices you can make and the sheer expansiveness of the game.

Fallout new vegas is a very good game. If your a fan of or interested in fallout games, its a perfect place to start/a good game to pickup.  I love how new vegas caters to those who prefer a holstered weapon, aswell as how many routes and endings you can take.

As someone who hates Fallout games, I loved this one. The writing in particular is what snagged me, but the creativity with some character and environment designs in what is otherwise an absolutely desolate desert also helped quite a bit. Would highly recommend both it and the DLCs if you want an interesting story with consequential actions you can take throughout and also if you've ever liked westerns. 

A note: this game is extremely buggy and will likely require looking some fixes up. If your save corrupts like mine repeatedly did at certain locations, I'll save you some time: make a new save, go through the tutorial, open the door of the starting house you're in, and save. From that save, load whichever one you were having trouble with, and it should work. No idea why it does that, but it worked for my playthrough.

Things like talking to an NPC could crash it, or you will be roaming the Mojave and all of a sudden, 'Woops my game crashed'. I did have it fatally crash once where it crashed my laptop once, but it hasn't happened again. Would recommend if your looking for a open world roleplay game. sorry if this is hard to read in any way shape or form, English is my fist language and I'm just stupid. Also 10 out of 10 I sexxed up Benny then strangled him in his bed.

Amazing & effective storytelling. Crazy & complex characters. 10/10 location & setting. Has decent amount of player freedom. Choices have a lasting impact. Tense & complicated faction conflict. Detailed & in-depth lore. Great music & soundtrack. World full of the most random stuff you can imagine. Funny as hell. Crashes a lot but who gives a sh*t. "What in the godd*mn...?" Best Fallout game.

Well, after playing this for the 50th time on every console possible I’ve done literally everything this game has to offer. All 4 endings, every single DLC, every Wild Wasteland easter egg, and every side quest on the map.

My favorite and once again latest playthrough is siding with the NCR, which basically means surviving a bullet to the skull just to become an unpaid, un-promoted intern for a corrupt military bureaucracy that taxes me for breathing.

What did i even do after playing the game completely over again and again..

    Spent 45 minutes spam-jumping up a vertical cliff face because taking the actual road meant fighting three Cazadores.

    Got stalked across three mountain ranges by Malcolm Holmes, who woke me up in the middle of the night just to talk about bottle caps.

    Got aggressively flirted with by a toaster in Old World Blues after floating brains stole my spine.

    Sat through a 3-hour slam poetry lecture about "the bear and the bull" from a guy in Lonesome Road just so I could headshot him with an Anti-Materiel Rifle.

    Crawled out of the Sierra Madre at 0.1 mph carrying 37 gold bars because I refused to "let go" like the game told me to. And yes i know you can put it in the bunker but what is the fun in that i wanted to see the dino again

The engine is like a school made game project let's be honest lol but luckily the steam deck runs it smooth as butter, despite it still crashing about 30 times in a span of 60 hours. It crashes if you look at a cactus too fast or jump down a cliff in the wrong way. and Boone routinely gives me cardiac arrest with a cinematic slow-mo killcam of a gecko he sniped from two zip codes away while I’m just trying to loot tin cans.

10/10. Patrolling the Mojave almost makes you wish for a nuclear winter. Or you know just for SOMEONE TO REMASTER THIS PLEASE but like in an actual beautiful re-engine work way not just a visual upgrade.. please Bethesda do us one favor

citations.review_text:
Never have written an "in-depth" review before, but here I go.

Fallout: New Vegas is a GREAT game in most of it's ways. The story is good, finding loot is good, the variety weapons are good (Silenced .45 auto FTW!), and all these places you can find are really good, even unmarked locations. This game is great with it's multiple choices for a different ending, and all the storytelling you can find EVERYWHERE. This game has it all if you like good narrative and fun gameplay. Only thing I really take issue with are the ridiculous bugs and crashes that happen sometimes, (And how Dead Money gets *harder* with more levels. Just do it at level 10 for maximum fun.) but that's New Vegas for ya. Unfortunately, due to this being a bit dated, this *DOES* require some modding to get it to work properly. That said, here's my manager and modlist:

Mod manager: Mod Organizer 2 (Mo2)

Mods: (Necessary)
NVSE
JIP LN NVSE PLUGIN
JohnnyGuitar NVSE
YUP - Base Game And All DLC
Stewie Tweaks
Stewie Tweaks - INI
UIO - User Interface Organizer
NVTF
NVTF - INI

 Note: For some of these mods, you will need a Nexus Account to download them.

(End of modlist)

This is my personal list, but you do what you want. Also, be sure to look up how to use BethINI and edit the INI files for optimized gameplay (don't forget to look for a more "official" modding guide!), and preferably get all DLC (Espescially GRA, Dead Money, and Lonesome Road). I don't care what people say, Dead Money and Lonesome Road are my favorite DLCs. 
Anyways, if you took the time to read all this, thank you, and BUY THE DARN GAME ALREADY!!! :)

Oh, and tell Oliver Swanick I said hi (after you buy the game)

🍰 This is my first ever game review on steam. Judging from this alone, you can tell how invested I was in the game. I played and finished it for 100+ hours and enjoyed immersing myself and understanding its lore. The music is also really catchy like 'Johnny Guitar' and 'Jingle Jangle Jingle'. My boyfriend recommended it to me and I couldn't be much happier to experience the world of fallout for the first time through New Vegas. Although, it's quite an old game with bugs and the occasional game crashing. However, I can say it was worth it, a classic Fallout story. if you love open world story games and exploration, with diverse characters give this game a try (ps. I would advice learning to mod it) ^_^
its a very good game with a great story, and great gameplay. the only negative thing about this game is that it crashes quite often, i would strongly reccomend downloading mods to fix the crashes.

Love this game! It blends FPS and RPG mechanics seamlessly and makes your choices feel like they actually have weight. The story is great and gives lots of room for you to explore different kinds of characters. The worst part about it is that it's over a decade old and needs a bunch of mods to keep it from crashing every twenty minutes.

Wow

No words could comprehend the writing of this game. Truly an experience worth checking out. 
Download the 4GB patcher mod on Nexus to avoid crashing. 
This has become my all-time favorite game. 
Geeked up playing Xbox all day.
Glory to Yes-man

i went into this fully blind and suffered through the first 10h of this game with crashes, not knowing that i was supposed to install "viva new vegas" to run this game as smooth as butter . and after installing that modpack ? boy did my life change .
this one is probably the best fallout game that i have played, captivating me with its stories, characters and gameplay features . i havent had this much fun with a rpg in such a long time !
go get the game, witness this masterpiece urself, its worth it . (and get the bundle so u have all the awesome dlcs too !)

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the extensive dialogue freedom, branching choices, and player agency that significantly impact quest outcomes and character interactions.

citations.review_text:
After spending an embarrassing amount of time with Fallout 4, I finally gave New Vegas a proper chance, and now I’m completely converted. The story is incredibly well written, the characters are unforgettable, the choices actually matter, and Boone is obviously the best companion ever created.

Everyone said it was the best Fallout game. I didn’t believe them.

I do now.

My only fear is that I’ll never find another game this good.
Possibly one of the best fallout games, you choices feel like they matter, Dont go to the seirra madre tho, terrible hotel, Ghosts attacked me

Love this game! It blends FPS and RPG mechanics seamlessly and makes your choices feel like they actually have weight. The story is great and gives lots of room for you to explore different kinds of characters. The worst part about it is that it's over a decade old and needs a bunch of mods to keep it from crashing every twenty minutes.

Fallout: New Vegas is the best true RPG experience you can have. I just finished the game with all the dlcs and most side content and HOLY SHII!!!! the amount of dialogue freedom you get is just staggering, it feels like I'm having an actual conversation with the npcs. I can have my character as evil as I want to be or I can be a fricking harbinger of peace. I can have good or bad relations with people and it affects the outcomes of quests. I swear even skyrim didn't feel as RPG as new vegas. I rate this game a 10/10 and a must play. For the best experience install the viva new vegas modlist and it's gonna make your playthrough 1000% better.

I'm just going through a new play through after at least 10 years since my last - graphics are aging at this point, and the story flow/NPC character depth is certainly aged compared to modern RPGs.  It's a little buggy with crashes after playing for a few hours (so save often).

But it's refreshing to play a game again that doesn't hold your hand too much.  One quickly gets over the older looking graphics.  The RPG open world exploration is still very enjoyable and challenging.  There are lots of options for how the end game plays out, and feels like your choices matter.
